flagged_defects_not_in_scope.description: On reflection this is NOT a logic bug: (year,month) path-based classification is the only reliable per-file date signal available -- this repo's reports/ tree includes one bulk historical reseed commit (08be801a, added 19,680 of ~19,955 files at once), so git-commit-date-based precision would be actively misleading, and filesystem mtimes reset on every checkout. Month granularity only ever widens the retention window, never narrows it below the configured day count, so it cannot archive something before it's genuinely eligible.
flagged_defects_not_in_scope.resolution: Docstring/comments updated to document this as intentional, conservative behavior rather than leaving it looking like an unexplained inconsistency. No logic change -- a day-precise rewrite would require abandoning the only trustworthy signal this repo's history provides.

flagged_defects_not_in_scope.description: Deliberately force-adds (git add -f) reports/ every pipeline run despite .gitignore:188, as an intra-run recovery safety net (restoring reports lost to a stash-pop mishap before the dist build). This is the root cause of ongoing reports/ growth (~240-380 files/day) and will regrow the directory after this one-time cleanup.

flagged_defects_not_in_scope.description: Two duplicate lines reading literal "*.md" (with quote characters included in the pattern) are a no-op -- git matches the pattern literally, not as a glob, so no .md file is actually ignored by this rule. Very likely why 283 loose .md files have accumulated at repo root over time.
flagged_defects_not_in_scope.recommended_action: NOT fixed this pass. The blast radius is unclear -- a repo-wide *.md ignore could affect legitimate future files (e.g. new CHANGELOG_vNN.md entries) if whatever process adds those doesn't force-add them, and that publishing path wasn't traced this session. Needs its own dedicated verification before touching.
